answer:
Two papers in the library are built around a preference-optimisation method that needs no reference model: **ORPO** and **SimPO**. A third, **KTO**, has a reference-free variant but only as a side experiment. All three are in `library/llm/post-training/preference-learning/`. I read the passages below in the papers themselves, not just the review.

### 1. ORPO: Monolithic Preference Optimization without Reference Model (Hong, Lee, Thorne, 2024)
- **What it is:** a "reference model-free monolithic odds ratio preference optimization algorithm" that removes the separate preference-tuning stage ([ORPO, p. 1, Abstract](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/ORPO.%20Monolithic%20Preference%20Optimization%20without%20Reference%20Model.pdf?page=1)).
- **How it works:** the loss is ordinary SFT plus a weighted penalty, $\mathcal{L}_{SFT} + \lambda\,\mathcal{L}_{OR}$. The penalty pushes up the odds of the chosen answer relative to the odds of the rejected one: $-\log\sigma\big(\log \tfrac{\text{odds}_\theta(y_w|x)}{\text{odds}_\theta(y_l|x)}\big)$. Only the model being trained appears in it ([p. 4, §4.2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/ORPO.%20Monolithic%20Preference%20Optimization%20without%20Reference%20Model.pdf?dest=subsection.4.2&page=4)).
- **Results:** Mistral-ORPO-β reaches 12.20% on AlpacaEval 2.0, against 10.99% for Zephyr-β. Most of the comparison models are official leaderboard entries rather than models the authors trained. Their own Llama-2 SFT+DPO baseline "could not be evaluated" ([p. 5, Table 1](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/ORPO.%20Monolithic%20Preference%20Optimization%20without%20Reference%20Model.pdf?dest=table.1&page=5)).

### 2. SimPO: Simple Preference Optimization with a Reference-Free Reward (Meng, Xia, Chen, 2024)
- **How it works:** in DPO's loss, the reward compares the policy's log-probability with the reference model's. SimPO replaces that with the length-averaged log-probability under the policy alone, $\tfrac{\beta}{|y|}\log\pi_\theta(y|x)$. This "eliminates the need for a reference model" ([SimPO, p. 3, §2.2](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/SimPO.%20Simple%20Preference%20Optimization%20with%20a%20Reference-Free%20Reward.pdf?dest=subsection.2.2&page=3)). It also adds a target margin γ to the Bradley–Terry objective ([p. 3–4, §2.3, Eq. 6](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/SimPO.%20Simple%20Preference%20Optimization%20with%20a%20Reference-Free%20Reward.pdf?dest=subsection.2.3&page=3)).
- **No KL term:** the loss has no KL penalty. The authors say a small learning rate, diverse data and the model's own robustness keep it close to where it started ([p. 4](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/SimPO.%20Simple%20Preference%20Optimization%20with%20a%20Reference-Free%20Reward.pdf?page=4&search=Preventing%20catastrophic%20forgetting)).
- **Results:** in its own tuned comparison, SimPO beats the best baseline by 3.6–4.8 points of length-controlled AlpacaEval 2 win rate ([p. 6, Table 4](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/SimPO.%20Simple%20Preference%20Optimization%20with%20a%20Reference-Free%20Reward.pdf?dest=table.4&page=6)).

### 3. KTO: Model Alignment as Prospect Theoretic Optimization (variant only)
- KTO's main method uses a reference model. As an ablation, the authors assume the reference is a uniform distribution, so it never has to be loaded into memory ([KTO, p. 8](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/KTO.%20Model%20Alignment%20as%20Prospect%20Theoretic%20Optimization.pdf?page=8&search=KTO%20works%20without%20a%20reference%20model)).
- That variant trails standard KTO and is more sensitive to its hyperparameters. The authors report that it "strictly outperforms ORPO" and uses less memory than any other method (same page).

### Did these methods hold up in other papers?
- **SimPO vs ORPO:** in SimPO's matched comparison, ORPO (and IPO and KTO) fall below plain DPO in nearly every setting ([SimPO, p. 6, Table 4](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/preference-learning/SimPO.%20Simple%20Preference%20Optimization%20with%20a%20Reference-Free%20Reward.pdf?dest=table.4&page=6)). The post-training review reads that table the same way, but I did not check every row myself.
- **SimPO in Tulu 3:** in Tulu 3's ablation, SimPO averages 51.8–52.9. That is below DPO at 55.2, below length-normalised DPO at 57.3, and even below the SFT starting point at 55.7 ([Tulu 3, p. 27, Table 18](http://pdf.invalid/llm/post-training/fine-tuning/Tulu%203.%20Pushing%20Frontiers%20in%20Open%20Language%20Model%20Post-Training.pdf?dest=table.18&page=27)).

I searched every paper in the library for reference-free wording. The other matches either just cite ORPO or SimPO or use "reference-free" in another sense, such as evaluation without a reference answer. Some RL papers drop the KL penalty, but they don't propose a preference-optimisation method, so I left them out.

Nothing in the library changed, so there's no commit to suggest.
